setting: First half: Inside garden path approaches willow on camera-right; low branch just beyond the family. Gate remains behind the camera. Second half: Same willow visitor path; meadow opens ahead, pale opaque wall stands on right beside tree as in proposed B119 anchor. Wall projected height alone does not prove it can conceal a nearby full-height giraffe. No giraffe or bird visible at final used frame; the bird perch may remain partly visible without bird.
lighting: Soft warm morning daylight; broad key from upper screen-left, gentle cream bounce fill, no hard rim or colored neon light. Stable white balance and exposure on peach skin and muted rose/dusty-teal/sage clothes; pale sky and restrained greens. Same light direction across cuts.
camera: First half: Rear-left follow slows with family; remain on path-left shoulder. Modest LEFT head glance toward mother may expose left profile. Do not require a frontal face or right cheek; keep parents and toddler visible. Second half: Hold the same left-shoulder camera through speech; track the last forward step on the same side. Do not swing to a new frontal view. Preserve the path-left camera side. Face visibility comes from a modest LEFT head turn toward mother, not from turning the torso away from the travel axis; never force full frontal face.
action: First half: Continue incoming forward stride and stop beneath willow. Toddler notices bird to the right with eyes/head, gently releases RIGHT hand from father and points with that free hand. LEFT hand stays with mother. Feet and torso stay aligned with path. During exact line1.00–3.47 turn head modestly LEFT toward mother, exposing a left partial profile to the rear-left camera; mother watches child then bird. After line look toward bird, without a body pivot or backward step. During final quiet interval after3.47s, smoothly return head and gaze toward bird; used119 targets the rear-pointing anchor, not the speech-profile anchor. Retain right pointing arm and mother hand contact. No body rotation, step back, or camera reset. Second half: Start from actual Aused119 rear-pointing state, head aimed toward bird. During local0–1s turn only head gently LEFT toward mother while pointing RIGHT remains unchanged. Deliver exact1.00–3.63 line in left partial profile; parents respond silently. After words return gaze forward-right, bird makes one small hop, lower RIGHT arm and take one gentle forward step with mother hand retained. Keep father hand free. Bird must leave view by actual trunk occlusion or upper-right frame edge; do not erase or move it onto another tree. End targets rear walking anchor with empty meadow, existing pale wall at right and willow trunk at right. No giraffe appears. All motion stays on original axis.
